title: exceptions.jsonl row (a person's waiver of one stop, or advice about one)
description: One row per stop a person authorised the session to go past, or per independent check of a stop, in .dabbler/runs/s<N>/exceptions.jsonl. A rule may be waived and a record may never be falsified: a waiver keeps the stop exactly as the framework wrote it -- the test failed, no verdict came, the check refused -- and adds that a person authorised going on, and why. It never says the gate was met, and nothing it covers is rewritten. A waiver is of THAT stop, matched on its kind and the time it was written: the next stop, or the same rule refusing a tree that has since moved, needs its own. Written only by the CLI (dabbler session waive), which an engine is refused. An advice row is what `dabbler triage` answered about a stop, or that its adviser could not be reached: marked as advice, it authorises nothing and no gate reads it.

stop.description: The stop advised on, copied from run.json as the framework wrote it: any kind, since a check may be asked of every stop.

reason.description: What was unmet, in the framework's words.

at.description: When the stop was written; what the loop matches the row to.

stop.description: The stop waived, copied from run.json as the framework wrote it.

kind.description: The kinds with something to go past. Every other stop has its own way on, and a waiver cannot make a push or a provider answer.

reason.description: What was unmet, in the framework's words.

at.description: When the stop was written; what the loop matches the waiver to.

reason.description: Why the person authorised going on, in their words. Permanent.

by.description: Who was working, as the session record from 'dabbler session start' says; written by the verb and never typed.

commit.description: HEAD when the waiver was given.

tree.description: The worktree snapshot when the waiver was given: the tree it lets through, and while the tree is still this one the waiver stands. A waiver is refused when the snapshot cannot be taken.

advice.description: This row is advice: an opinion about the stop, never a decision, and nothing reads it as one.

adviser.description: Who answered, and the provider they were reached on; null where nobody could be reached.

simulated.description: Served by a script rather than a vendor.

answer.description: The adviser's answer, as triage.schema.json validated it on arrival; null where the adviser could not be reached or its answer could not be used.

unreachable.description: Why no usable answer came, where none did: nobody could be reached (the adviser is null), or the named adviser's answer could not be used (the answer is null).
